current.text: He is the starting center on offense in Washington. Alex Sarr starts next to him and plays more power forward.
He projects to play about 32 minutes a game.
He missed many games last season. Some of the absences in Washington were partly not real injuries.
Do not expect 75 games. If he plays about 60 games, a pick in the mid 20s is a good one. At 62 games he would be a tier three or four center.
Per game he could rank about 14th and has top 10 upside.

Experts value him around picks 21 to 26. They call his slide to Yahoo rank 45 and ADP near 43 an overreaction and would take him in round 3. One expert would still call him an easy pick in round 4 of a 12 team league.
He is a value at his Yahoo rank. Do not draft him at his ESPN rank of 14.
In an auction, one expert values him at 30 USD per game but would buy him only at a discount. He went for 26 USD in that mock auction.
If you pair him with Wembanyama, blocks and rebounds are strong, but you then need guard stats.

Experts expect Washington to keep him and push for the playoffs. One puts it at about 80%. A trade, with Golden State rumored, cannot be ruled out, and the team could reconsider around the trade deadline.
He and Trae Young are expected to get Washington's preferred offensive touches.
Washington has only 14 back-to-backs this season and one in the fantasy playoffs.
Washington is trying to compete, with a projection of about 40 wins and a play-in spot. Late-season resting and minutes cuts are not expected. His health is a key factor for the team.

durable.text: He has repeated lower-body injuries of several different kinds. In Dallas he never played five games in a row before getting hurt.
Expect missed games every season. Experts have low confidence in his lower body.
He is 33. He can still produce when he is on the floor.
His outside shooting and perimeter game decline every year. He now rarely shoots anything except at the rim.
One expert rates his rim protection below Alex Sarr's.
Rebounds and blocks are league outliers, and they carry his category value.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.
As an often-injured player, he can go a bit earlier in roto than in head-to-head.

note: Per game he is an elite rebounds and blocks source with strong FG% and points, so his only real question is games played. Sites project 58 to 61 games. Experts value him at 30 USD per game but want a discount. Yahoo's value of 23 USD and the 26 USD mock price are a fair target range, well below the 54 USD he cost in our league last season and the ESPN value of 46 USD. He fits big-man builds, for example with Wembanyama, as long as you add guard stats and threes. Early in the season, check how many games in a row he plays and whether the trade rumors with Golden State return.
